subject: [hw] opus-dec3 -> lead: final installed plug-in set (encoders + decoders), ids, ranking, switches - proposal for decision
body:
Constraint [V]: VideoToolbox dlopens exactly ONE free path per kind, each with a fixed entry: /System/Library/VideoEncoders/Slim.videoencoder -> SLIMEncoderRegister, /System/Library/VideoDecoders/Slim.videodecoder -> SLIMRegister (5th in the decoder list). So "one dylib per codec" is not possible: all encoders share one file and all decoders share one file.

Proposal: TWO dylibs, one source tree.
 A) Slim.videoencoder (exists, proven): n2vt_shim.c + n2vt_log.c + n2avc + n2jpeg + P04 (annexb, n2hwenc_vt, n2hwenc_client, n2hwenc_register) + P03 client statically linked. Entry SLIMEncoderRegister.
 B) Slim.videodecoder (new, DEC06): its own small shim exporting SLIMRegister + n2vt_log.c + DEC06 object + the same P03 client. Separate file so that (1) deleting it is a complete decoder off switch without touching recording, (2) a decoder crash or bad registration cannot break the proven encoder registration, (3) the two can be staged/rolled back independently by the installer (owned-video.json gets the second path). Both are loaded into the same processes (mediaserverd hosts encode and decode sessions for apps [V for decode: VTDecompressionSessionRemote]); two statically linked client copies are fine (no shared state; each opens /dev/redwood-vcodec-client itself).

Registrations and ordering (VT sorts: Rating desc, then hardware first, then ID; CreateInstance errors fall through for both; StartSession errors fall through for ENCODERS only) [V]:
 encoders  avc1: com.nord2.videotoolbox.videoencoder.avc1.n2hw  HW=true  Rating 100   (P04, only with claim-hw)
                 com.nord2.videotoolbox.videoencoder.avc1.n2avc HW=claim-hw  rating 0 (software fallback)
           hvc1/hev1: ...hvc1.n2hw HW=true Rating 100 (P04, claim-hw)  then ...hvc1.vcp (Apple VCPHEVC software) HW=claim-hw
           jpeg: ...jpeg.n2jpeg (unchanged)
 decoders  avc1/hvc1: com.nord2.videotoolbox.videodecoder.mtkvdec(.avc1/.hvc1 appended by VT) HW=true Rating 100,
           fallback = Apple H264SW / VCPHEVC (HW=false, rating 0, already registered by VT itself).
 => Camera recording picks P04 when vcodecd answers, n2avc otherwise; playback picks MTK VDEC when CreateInstance's HELLO succeeds, Apple software otherwise.

Switches (files, read once per process):
 nord2-video-off           everything off (both dylibs)
 nord2-video-claim-hw      software encoders claim HW AND P04 is registered (one switch, so the RequireHW fallback is always there)
 nord2-video-hwdec         decoder registered (new, in include/n2vt_dec_abi.h as a proposal); nord2-video-hwdec-no-hevc
 (existing no-avc / no-hevc / no-jpeg / quiet unchanged)
After M4c (VENC proven on the phone) I recommend P04 registration default-on (drop the claim-hw condition for P04 only), since the StartSession retry is [V]; the cost of a dead daemon is then one connect timeout (2 s with my patch 1) per session creation.

Open points needing your decision: (1) OK to add the two decoder switch constants (they live in hwcodec/include/n2vt_dec_abi.h now, not in the frozen n2vt_abi.h)? (2) who owns the decoder shim + build line (IP's build_ios.sh, PLUGIN_OBJS style) and the installer entry (gpu/video/install owned-video.json + guest-video.sh)? (3) sandbox: first phone run of either hardware path must check that mediaserverd can open /dev/redwood-vcodec-client (if not: a kernel sandbox exception, or vcodecd-side relay via a mach service).
